selection: Super Lube 21030, NLGI 2, 85 g tube: an ordinary candidate for the tripod's all-purpose grease requirement, not an identified paper product or an Onset-approved substitution.

sources.locator: PDF page 5: 21030 row, 3 oz / 85 g tube and adjacent tube photograph
sources.visual_inspection: Page and native tube photograph inspected. Silver-grey tapered tube, flat sealed hanging flange, pale ribbed cap. No dimensional drawing.

sources.locator: Pages 1–3: no silicone; 21030 NLGI 2 tube; translucent white; specific gravity 0.89 at 60 F; clean application surface
Sections 6–8: closed storage, contamination control, absorbent collection and spill cleanup
Page 1 lists all-purpose grease; page 8 lightly greases the creased upper end of the lower mast
Adding/removing sensors and installation instructions specify silicone grease for cable channels. This is a different consumable requirement.

reconstruction.dimension_status: Selected photo-proportion and capacity hypothesis, not manufacturer dimensions or a measured package
reconstruction.thread_status: External helical ridge with a female clearance envelope; pitch, local dimensions and sealing construction are inferred. No thread engagement qualification.
reconstruction.cad_status: No official or licensed CAD retrieved. Original authored geometry and identification text; no manufacturer artwork redistributed.
reconstruction.material_volume_basis: 85 g / approximate density 0.89 g/mL = 95.5056 mL. Approximates water reference density as 1 g/mL; not a package volume claim.

usage_limits: Selected only for the metal mast joint. Product compatibility and required application mass remain unverified; the 2 g application allowance is an explicit inventory inference from a 0.1 mm film on the selected joint envelope plus losses.
Do not allocate this silicone-free grease to U30 cable-channel sealing; separately sourced silicone grease is still missing.
Do not convert catalogue lubricity into a simulation friction coefficient without calibration.
Ordinary applicator, cleaning/absorbent stock, campaign consumption and residual/waste accounting remain to be allocated.
